summary: White Oak Mountain tower near Waldron: a 48-foot tower nearly complete in 1928, an 85-foot steel tower described in 1971, removed note in 1974; summit now a Forest Service electronic site.

facts.design: 1928 item: 48-foot lookout tower; 1971 Forest Service station description: four-legged steel tower with a metal cabin, 85 feet overall
facts.status_note: The only removal note is '1974: Removed' on a page that covers both candidate towers without naming one; no source says what became of the 85-foot tower after 1971; the summit now hosts communications sites
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (per the 1971 station description); Ouachita National Forest (page heading); the station is on property the state leases

access.note: No source read describes public access to the summit; Forest Service notices list communications sites under special use authorizations

corrections.why: The only removal note is '1974: Removed' and it does not name a tower. The 1971 station describes an 85-foot tower whose later fate is not given. The 48-foot 1928 tower may be gone, but the record mixes it with the 85-foot station.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Central lookouts page heading says Scott County, Ouachita National Forest, near Waldron. The 1971 station record says AR/FRANKLIN. Not reconciled; the story reports both.
The brief's 14.6 m equals 48 feet, the 1928 tower. The 1971 station description gives 85 feet overall. The story reports both figures.
The page groups the 1928 tower and the 1971 station under one White Oak Mountain heading. No source read says they are the same structure.

notes_for_editor: The record appears to mix two structures. Its coordinates (35.562782, -93.708212) seem to match the 1971 station description, which is 6 miles north and 14 miles west of Clarksville and 5 miles north and 7 miles east of Ozark, by a rough check against town locations; its 14.6 m height and 'gone' status match the 1928 48-foot tower and the 1974 note; its county 'Scott' matches the page heading. An editor should decide whether to split this into two records. The OSM node was not fetched. One WebSearch summary mentioned an underground powerline proposal at the summit electronic site; I did not find that notice in the archive grep, so it is not used. The archive is one long listing; the individual notices have no URLs captured. No photos added.
